frozenQuestion: Does one standardized prior injury change full-population recovery from a second matched injury through retained native state, structural preconditioning, or movement-dependent fatigue, after retaining every first-stage failure and censor?

inherits.checkpointState: occupancy, Selection cursors, activation count/global event clock, stream counters, native ledger, and S04 fatigue state

population.estimandPopulation: all 384 validated S02 checkpoints without conditioning on first-injury recovery

sequenceAssignment.ownership: construction-only counter-addressed assignment; never enters runtime stream counters
sequenceAssignment.blocking: within each S01 pairing block, sort the eight timing conditions by one counter-addressed uint64 and assign four to each sequence

sequences.severity: centered 20%-scale window; affected count fixed by n; target-state inversion addition C(k,2)
two centered adjacent equal 10%-scale blocks; affected count fixed by n; target-state inversion addition b^2

sequenceAssignment.poolingRule: operator-stratified primary estimates; no scalar severity equivalence is asserted across operators

postRecoveryStabilization.rule: after first target attainment and before assigned spacing, preserve S01's charged uniform-scheduler achieved-state certificate
postRecoveryStabilization.uniformCoverageRule: at least two scheduled opportunities per identity
postRecoveryStabilization.success: zero target distance, native absorbing-occupancy certificate, complete actor coverage, and no accepted movement
postRecoveryStabilization.failureHandling: retain as a first-stage competing terminal; episode 2 remains unobservable

excluded: all S08 plastic modes because none was validated and four harmed recovery
S09 target-aware controllers because S10 retains the original target and S09 did not establish learning
S07 local-memory variants as validated benefits because S07 was null against matched controls

arms.sequence: active assigned injury, retained fatigue/state, active same injury
sham first injury, donor-duration native exposure, active assigned second injury
arms.role: naive control matched to the paired donor's pre-second opportunity clock

arms.sequence: same as naive, then replace fatigue load and residual cooldown vector with the paired donor snapshot before the second injury
arms.role: post-treatment mediator benchmark; descriptive, not a total-effect control

arms.sequence: active assigned injury, no fatigue overlay, active same injury
active assigned injury, retained fatigue/state, sham second injury plus 20*n stability probe
arms.role: appropriate no-second-injury stability and cost control

stateContract.priorInjury: never reset occupancy, Selection cursors, global event index, stream counters, ledger, or fatigue state between episodes
stateContract.rest: after exact S01 post-recovery stabilization, charge ordinary uniform-scheduler target-stable opportunities; target departure is a validation failure and makes episode 2 unobservable
stateContract.fatigueMatching: copy the paired donor's per-identity load and residual cooldown vector at the second-injury boundary using a frozen same-case rule independent of control outcomes
stateContract.structuralPreconditioning: episode 2 is administered only from the exact original target occupancy; all other first-stage outcomes remain explicit competing terminals
stateContract.longitudinalEnvelope: phase-local budgets are enforced independently beyond the original single-repair Scenario envelope without changing the original scenario ID or RNG root

primary: jointSequenceSuccess over the full assigned population
episode2ObservationRisk over the full assigned population
all-population restricted episode-2 opportunity time with first-stage competing terminals fixed at the phase budget
cause-specific terminal counts: episode1 competing terminal, episode2 completion, episode2 quiescence, episode2 phase budget, and no-second control
secondary: episode-specific distance AUC and accepted swaps
fatigue loads, cooldowns, triggers, blocks, and recoveries
target-stable rest and no-second stability departures
outcomes.conditionalAnalysis: second-stage summaries among observed episode-2 cases are supplementary and explicitly post-treatment selected
outcomes.missingObservability: never substitute, exclude, or classify an unadministered second injury as an ordinary second-stage censor

estimands.experience: paired prior-injury versus opportunity-matched naive difference in full-population joint success and restricted episode-2 time, stratified by sequence and spacing
estimands.fatigue: paired retained-fatigue versus fatigue-disabled and fatigue-state-matched benchmarks; fatigue matching is descriptive mediation evidence
estimands.hysteresis: any prespecified full-population second-episode difference after prior injury relative to naive under the same assigned injury and spacing
estimands.learning: requires multiplicity-adjusted improvement over naive at immediate spacing and retained same-direction improvement after 100*n rest, with no joint-success harm; otherwise learning is not claimed

multiplicity.primaryFamily: two injury sequences by three spacings by two experience controls
multiplicity.method: Holm adjustment across all prespecified paired completion tests
multiplicity.durationTest: two-sided exact sign test on nonzero all-population restricted-time differences

claimBoundary: Repeated injury, experience, fatigue, hysteresis, and learning are operational simulator terms. No learning is claimed without prespecified improvement plus long-rest retention, and no result is biological evidence.
